第一条: Article 1  These Regulations are formulated in order to standardise order in the telecommunications market, to protect the lawful rights and interests of telecommunications users and telecommunications business operators, to safeguard the security of telecommunications networks and information, and to promote the healthy development of the telecommunications industry.
第二条:
Article 2  Any party engaging in telecommunications activities, or activities related to telecommunications, within the territory of the People’s Republic of China must comply with these Regulations.

“Telecommunications” in these Regulations means the activity of transmitting, emitting or receiving voice, text, data, images or information in any other form by means of wired or wireless electromagnetic systems or opto-electronic systems.
第三条:
Article 3  The competent information industry department of the State Council exercises supervision and administration over the national telecommunications industry in accordance with these Regulations.

The telecommunications administrations of the provinces, autonomous regions and directly governed municipalities exercise supervision and administration over the telecommunications industry within their respective administrative areas, in accordance with these Regulations and under the leadership of the competent information industry department of the State Council.
第四条:
Article 4  The supervision and administration of telecommunications follows the principles of separating government from enterprise, breaking monopoly, encouraging competition and promoting development, and of openness, fairness and impartiality.

A telecommunications business operator shall conduct its business in accordance with law, observe commercial ethics, and submit to supervision and inspection carried out in accordance with law.
第五条: Article 5  A telecommunications business operator shall provide telecommunications users with telecommunications services that are prompt, accurate, secure, convenient and reasonably priced.
第六条: Article 6  The security of telecommunications networks and information is protected by law. No organisation or individual may use a telecommunications network to engage in activities endangering national security, the public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others.
